title: Price-Fixing Cartels and Firm Innovation
eligible_reason: Binary treatment (firm participates in a price-fixing cartel) switching on at cartel-specific formation years (24 distinct formation years, 1976-2005, across 49 cartels and 353 treated patenting firms in the formation sample), never-treated controls (77,162 other patenting assignees), firm fixed effects and 4-digit-NAICS-industry-by-year fixed effects (time-invariant characteristic x calendar time, allowed), no covariates, clustered by industry: felm(depvar ~ TreatY + TreatY:POST | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl). Event-study versions use TreatY:TimeFromYY relative-year factors with -1 omitted. Sample restrictions: treated firms are kept only within relative years -4..4 and only before the cartel breaks up (TimeToY <= -1 or missing in the formation file), controls are kept in all years. R&D specifications use the same structure on a Compustat firm-year file (gvkey, cl x fyear FE). Panel (b) of each table studies cartel breakup as the event (POST switches on at the dissolution year with the collusion years as pre-period); these are recorded as eligible reverse-event specifications and flagged. Figure 4(b)/(d) 3-year-bin event studies span both formation and breakup and need the post-breakup bins dropped under the switch-off rule.
design_notes: Replicate.R (lfe::felm). Patent files: data_reg_patent_from.rds (432,448 firm-years; TreatY==1 rows 1,603 for 353 firms; TimeFromYY factor -4..-1, 1..4 with 1 = formation year; controls carry placeholder TimeFromYY = -2 so POST = 0), data_reg_patent_to.rds (465 treated firms, 31 distinct breakup years 1977-2015; TimeToY -4..-1, 1..4 with 1 = breakup year), data_reg_patent_to_ext.rds (window -2..6), data_reg_patent.rds (TimeGroup 3-year bins across formation and breakup), *_competitors.rds and *_others.rds (TreatN exposure for non-colluding firms). cl equals the first four digits of naics6_gra1 (260 industries, 83 with treated firms); no firm appears in more than one cl and TreatY is constant within firm, so cl x year is a plain industry-by-year FE (not a stacked design). R&D file data_reg_rnd.rds: 14,691 gvkeys, 72 cl groups, 56 treated gvkeys, TimeFromY coded with 0 = formation year, controls placeholder -1; samples drop relative year -1 (formation) or 0 (breakup) and remove singleton gvkeys. Outcomes are inverse-hyperbolic-sine transformed counts. Treated firms are observed 1-8 years in the formation window (101 firms only once). Figures 1-3 descriptive; Figure 5 permutation inference; Table 1 descriptives; Table 3 leave-one-out.
n_eligible_specs_note: Counts every main-text column/bar/event-study path with the TreatY(TreatN):POST or relative-time structure: Table 2 (16), Figure 4 (6), Figure 6 (12), Figure 7 (9), Table 4 (8), Table 5 (4), Table 6 (12). 26 of these are breakup (reverse-event) specifications; 8 use non-colluding competitor/other-firm exposure (TreatN).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 24 distinct cartel-formation years (1976-2005) among treated firms in data_reg_patent_from.rds (largest cohorts: 2000 (74 firms), 1998 (43), 2002 (30), 1989 (21)); 31 distinct breakup years in data_reg_patent_to.rds; R&D file has 56 treated gvkeys.
modern_estimator_note: Full text cites Baker, Larcker and Wang (2022) per candidate flags; code uses felm TWFE only.

published_estimates.statistic: abstract: colluding firms exhibited increases of 28% in patent filings (IHS coefficient approx. log(1.28) = 0.25)

data_access: partial (final cleaned and merged regression files shipped as .rds; raw PatentsView, Compustat (licensed) and DOJ/VitalLaw cartel data not included)
data_files_note: README.pdf: 'all figures and tables can be reproduced using the codes and datasets provided here'; data are real processed values (not synthetic). Note Replicate.R lines 378-381 read the competitors/others files without the Data/ prefix; they are located in Data/.
software_notes: R 4.1.1 with data.table, lfe (felm), broom, ggplot2, tidyverse. README recommends 32 GB RAM; loading takes minutes, regressions under a minute.
priority_note: Eligible, data and code complete, R. Caveats for re-estimation: industry-by-year FE (cl x year) must be carried into CSA/BJS as group-by-time FE; treated units are trimmed to an 8-year window while controls span 1976-2020 (unbalanced); breakup specifications are reverse events; TreatY main effect is collinear with firm FE.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Data structure verified in R: no assignee or gvkey appears in more than one cl; TreatY constant within unit; cl == substr(naics6_gra1,1,4) for 100% of rows in the patent files; formation years computed from TimeFromYY==1, breakup years from TimeToY==1. Table/column numbers follow the section comments in Replicate.R (Table 2 columns 1-16, Table 4 columns 1a-4b, Table 5 columns 1-4, Table 6 columns 1a-6b); verify against the published article when text is available.
